mentions.name: Bonsai
mentions.description: A voxel game engine in development for ~10 years that represents worlds as collections of SDFs (density fields). The world generator and editor run almost entirely on the GPU via a three-stage pipeline: a user-configurable GLSL 'shaping' shader, a fused stage that computes normals, runs a user-configurable 'decoration' function and applies SDF edits compiled from a graph structure into bytecode, and a final convolution/packing stage producing 32-bit occupancy, color, and normal per voxel. The entire pipeline is a single fused 'ubershader' dispatched three times to keep driver overhead near zero. GPU results are passed back to the CPU for entity/structure spawning callbacks, then meshed with a fast binary meshing algorithm; surface chunks store 16 bits per voxel (1 occupancy bit, 15 normal bits) and scale to worlds larger than 1B voxels cubed. Profiling shows ~500B-1T perlin samples per second on a 3080ti mobile, with headroom from 16/8-bit textures. Designed to give users easy-to-use tools plus granular control over final output.

mentions.name: Bonsai
mentions.description: A voxel game engine developed over ~10 years and written entirely from scratch, including memory allocators, font rasterizer, collision detection, and the simulation loop, with the C runtime as its only external dependency. Worlds and most things in them are represented as collections of SDFs (density fields), and a world edit is defined by SDF parameters that are rasterized into the voxel grid by a GPU shader, supporting smooth unions with rounded contours. It centers on an editor and is nearing completion of a major rewrite, with plans to build games on top of it in closed-source repos.
